summary: The note explains resilience as a learnable skill that helps high school teens recover from setbacks and adapt to adversity. It reviews six strategies: supportive community, positive thinking, emotional regulation, problem-solving, physical self-care, and learning from failure. Each is tied to a local program or professional active since September 2023.
one_line: Overview of six strategies for building teen resilience, each linked to local programs and professionals who have been active since late 2023.
key_facts: Resilience is the ability to bounce back from negative experiences and adapt to difficult situations; it can be learned and developed by anyone.

The 'Strong Minds, Strong Futures' program was unveiled on September 12, 2023, by child psychologist Dr. Samantha Lee, providing resilience resources and training for students and educators across the region.
Jordan Matthews, a high school guidance counselor, has set up peer mentoring programs in local schools since October 2023.
Matthews says teens should have at least one person to turn to when struggling: 'The foundation of resilience is knowing that you're not alone.'
The 'Positive Teens' initiative was launched in November 2023 by educator Amanda Richardson and integrates positive psychology principles into the school curriculum.
Michael Thomson, a local youth counselor working with adolescents since the start of 2024, promotes emotional regulation techniques such as mindfulness, deep breathing, and journaling.
Lisa Wong has promoted life skills classes since late September 2023, using collaborative projects that mimic real-world problems to build problem-solving skills and confidence.
The 'Healthy Minds in Healthy Bodies' campaign has been championed by fitness coach Tyler Evans since January 2024 and links physical well-being to mental strength.
Evans says 'Exercise is a known stress-buster, and a healthy body often means a more resilient mind.'
Dr. Nina Patel has offered workshops since February 2024 to destigmatize failure and promote a growth mindset in high schoolers.
Patel says 'Failure is not the opposite of success; it's a stepping stone towards it.'

The note concludes that fostering resilience needs a multifaceted approach combining social support, positive thinking, emotional regulation, problem-solving, self-care, and a healthy view of failure.
